submission.bindingBasis: The planning-time sourceStateDigest (sha256:e5d8008d...) no longer matches the current sourceStateDigest (sha256:79bcb09f...). The difference is an empty Git commit, but the tree bytes are identical. A re-observation would produce the new exact current digest, against which workspace.close can compare-and-close under the owner contract's post-observation clause.
submission.rationale: The planning binding attempt failed with REVISION_MISMATCH/not_committed because the HEAD revision advanced (cc96f434... vs 4e6ce637...) even though the tree bytes are byte-identical. The owner contract states that after re-observation a caller may close against the new exact current digest. Since the tree content is unchanged, re-observing will yield a fresh digest matching the current state, allowing workspace.close to commit. This preserves the intended consequence (close the workspace and release its local materialization) rather than holding or abandoning. ACT_UNBOUND would violate the compare-and-close contract, and ACT_WITH_PLANNING_BINDING is impossible since the planning digest is stale. REOBSERVE_THEN_DECIDE is the correct middle path that lets us re-validate against the current state before acting.
